definition: A free operant is a behavioral procedure in which a response can be made at any time rather than only when a specific trial is presented. In the temporal avoidance form described here, an animal can respond freely to prevent an aversive event that would occur if too much time passes without that response.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence claims that a free operant is a procedure where a response can be made “at any time rather than only when a specific trial is presented.” This specific characterization is not stated in the provided packet text.

The packet only explicitly describes free-operant temporal avoidance (Sidman avoidance) in which an animal receives a shock if an interval passes without a specified response; the “trial presented” contrast is not supported.
The first sentence adds a general procedural contrast (“rather than only when a specific trial is presented”) that is not supported by the packet.
The packet supports free-operant temporal avoidance as a timed avoidance procedure, but it does not define the broader term as a response available at any time independent of trial presentation.
